children: German industry got off to a weak start in the third quarter, even though the decline may primarily attributable to a one-time effect in auto production, Commerzbank economist Ralph Solveen says in a note. Output fell 1.1% in July, with a temporary stoppage to retool a car plant for e-vehicle manufacturing driving a 9.2% drop in car production, data agency Destatis said. "However, even without this effect, production would continue to trend downward," Solveen says. With low water levels on German rivers also hampering production in August, the German economy is likely to expand at a slower pace in the third quarter than it did in previous quarters, he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
